claims.text: SPS at approximately 2000 °C with a 3–5 minute isothermal hold will fully densify single-phase ZrB2.
The proposed SPS treatment will ensure phase-pure ZrB2.
Rapid SPS with a brief isothermal hold will reduce porosity in ZrB2.
Rapid sintering and the controlled hold will minimize ZrB2 grain growth.
The controlled hold will seal open pores and produce a denser ZrB2 microstructure with fewer flaws.
Pulsed direct current during SPS enables fast diffusive mass transport in ZrB2.
A 3–5 minute hold at approximately 2000 °C provides enough time for complete phase transformation.
The proposed SPS schedule suppresses excessive grain growth and pore connectivity.
Reduced pore connectivity makes the ceramic less susceptible to infiltration by the liquid plating bath.
Reduced liquid infiltration will reduce subsequent ceramic degradation.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have lower overall porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2 prepared above 2300 °C.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have a finer microstructure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have a more uniform microstructure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 will have higher mechanical strength than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
After 1000 hours in a 120 °C liquid plating bath, SPS-processed ZrB2 will exhibit less hole formation than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
After 1000 hours in a 120 °C liquid plating bath, SPS-processed ZrB2 will exhibit fewer structural failures than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 sintered above 2300 °C with prolonged dwell times typically has higher porosity and larger grains.
The higher porosity and larger grains attributed to conventional ZrB2 reduce its mechanical integrity during prolonged service.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary state categorically that the proposed process will fully densify the ceramic and ensure phase purity, whereas the uncertainty field acknowledges that uniform phase purity and densification may not be reproducible across batches.
